$comment: Golden cases for GSTIN validation. Every check character below was computed with the GSTN base-36 algorithm and is correct; the PANs are invented. Messages are pinned in full, not matched loosely: a message that stops naming the character position stops being useful to the person typing, and that regression should fail a test rather than pass one.

valid.why: check character is a digit, not a letter
check character is Z, the same letter as the fixed position 14
all-zero PAN digits — a base-36 value of 0 contributes nothing to the sum
character 13 is '2' — a second registration for the same PAN in the same state
a union territory that levies SGST, because it has a legislature
a union territory that levies UTGST
offshore areas — a code that is valid in a GSTIN but not offered in a picker
centrally administered, and likewise not a place of supply
a retired code still has to validate — it is on documents already issued
lower case is a keyboard state, not a mistake
spaces anywhere: this is how a GSTIN arrives when it is read off a certificate

invalid.why: whitespace only, which normalises to empty

invalid.message: A GSTIN is 15 characters long. This one has 14.
invalid.why: one short — the state code is still readable, so it is still reported

invalid.message: A GSTIN is 15 characters long. This one has 16.
invalid.why: one too many, the usual result of a double keystroke

invalid.message: A GSTIN is 15 characters long. This one has 1.
invalid.why: too short to carry a state code at all

invalid.message: A GSTIN starts with a two-digit state code, for example 33 for Tamil Nadu. This one starts with 'A3'.
invalid.why: letters where the state code goes

invalid.message: Characters 3 to 7 are the five letters that start the PAN, for example ABCDE. This one has 'AAB1C'.
invalid.why: a digit inside the PAN letters — 1 typed for I

invalid.message: Characters 8 to 11 are the four digits of the PAN. This one has '12A4'.
invalid.why: a letter inside the PAN digits

invalid.message: Character 12 is the last letter of the PAN. This one has '4'.
invalid.why: the PAN's check letter typed as a digit

invalid.message: Character 13 says which registration this is for the PAN in that state, a letter or a digit. This one has '-'.
invalid.why: punctuation where the registration number goes

invalid.message: Character 14 of every GSTIN is the letter Z. This one has 'Y'.
invalid.why: the fixed Z mistyped — adjacent key

invalid.message: The last character is a check character, a letter or a digit. This one has '-'.
'88' is not an Indian state code. A GSTIN starts with the state code, for example 33 for Tamil Nadu.
invalid.why: structurally perfect, checksum correct, and still not a real state — the check character cannot catch this

invalid.message: '00' is not an Indian state code. A GSTIN starts with the state code, for example 33 for Tamil Nadu.
invalid.why: 00 looks like a state code and is not one

invalid.message: The last character does not match the rest of this GSTIN, so at least one character is mistyped. Check it against the registration certificate.
invalid.why: check character wrong, everything else right

invalid.message: The last character does not match the rest of this GSTIN, so at least one character is mistyped. Check it against the registration certificate.
invalid.why: one character of the PAN mistyped — this is what the checksum is for

invalid.message: The last character does not match the rest of this GSTIN, so at least one character is mistyped. Check it against the registration certificate.
invalid.why: two digits transposed, the mistake a format check alone cannot see

invalid.message: The last character does not match the rest of this GSTIN, so at least one character is mistyped. Check it against the registration certificate.
invalid.why: right GSTIN, wrong state code pasted in front of it
